title: Nebula Finance - Redwood Console Tracing & Request Logs Debugging Demo
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Nebula Finance through the Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs debugging flows. Customer is evaluating for production inference (dedicated vs hosted) with strict security requirements (SSO/SAML, KMS). Main asks: retention for request logs, RBAC on traces, ability to link request logs to Kibana/SIEM, and running live debug on sample failing requests. Agreed next steps: share security pack, run a short benchmark, provide pricing for a pilot (3-month dedicated pool).

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Ava (Redwood SE), Jordan (CS), Maya, Daniel, Priya, Ethan (Nebula)

Summary: (auto) demo of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs with live debugging flow.

---
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. We got about an hour. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood, with Ava our SE who will walk through tracing and request logs. Jordan from CS is on too. Maya, Daniel, Priya — thanks for being here.
[00:18] Maya: Hey Samir, thanks, yeah excited. We wanted to focus on error analysis and how we can root cause failing generations.
[00:25] Ava (Redwood SE): Great, that's exactly what I planned to show — tracing, request logs, and the debugging replay flow. Quick question before we start — are you leaning towards Dedicated or Hosted for the pilot?
[00:38] Daniel: We're evaluating both. Concern is latency vs cost. For prod we probably need Dedicated but want to test Hosted first for speed of onboarding. Also security is big — S S O / S A M L integration, KMS for keys, and retention limits.
[00:55] Samir: Totally. For Dedicated we can pin capacity and get predictable latency. For Hosted we have encryption at rest and KMS integrations, and we can provide SOC2 docs — I'll share the pack after.
[01:10] Ava: Ok jumping into the console — I'm sharing my screen — (link: deck/demo-notes) — first up the Tracing tab. You'll see per-request flame graph, token timing, and error markers. Note: the auto-detected spans sometimes label 'kv cache' as 'K V cache' in the UI — it's an AG auto-tokenization quirk.
[01:35] [screen showing traces] Ava: Here's a request where latency spiked at token 42; you can expand spans to see kernel selection and the routing path — we show GPU selection (a100/rtx), quantization profile used, and whether prefix caching hit.
[01:51] Daniel: The trace looks useful. Can we link that to our Kibana logs or SIEM? We need to ingest all traces for compliance.
[02:00] Ava: Yes, we have a webhook export and S3 export for request logs. Logs include request_id, timestamps, model, model_version, cost_estimate, user-provided metadata. You can forward to S3 then to your SIEM. We also have a request-logs API.
[02:15] Priya: About retention — what's default? We can't keep PII for more than 30 days.
[02:20] Samir: Default hosted retention is 90 days, but for Dedicated/private we can configure retention and provide custom policies. For pilot we can set 30 days and document controls.
[02:32] Maya: Also RBAC — can we limit who sees request contents vs just metadata?
[02:36] Ava: Yes, RBAC supports roles: trace-viewer (metadata only), trace-debugger (full content), admin. SAML/SSO mapping can be done to groups. Occasionally the S S O mapping in the UI shows group names truncated — small UI bug we have a fix for.
[02:53] [00:03:00] Ava: Now Error Analysis tab — we surface common failure modes: truncated responses, hallucination flags (auto-eval with prompt set), server-side model timeouts, and model output validation errors. Here's a failure cluster where many requests hit a model timeout at 10s.
[03:15] Daniel: How do you determine whether it's a model or infra issue?
[03:19] Ava: We correlate the trace spans with kernel-level metrics and queue depth; if the kernel times are low but queue depth is high it's an infra queuing problem. If kernel time is high with low queue depth, it's likely model comp or sequence-length heavy.
[03:33] Samir: We also have automatic fallback — if a request hits an error threshold we can reroute to a smaller model or to a dedicated fallback pool. That helps availability.
[03:45] Ethan: For debugging, can you replay a request with the same KV cache state? We saw differences between replay and live.
[03:52] Ava: Great question — yes, we capture KV cache snapshots for replayable sessions, but note that cross-request state and time-dependent system prompts can make exact parity hard. We'll ask for the failing request IDs and we'll run a controlled replay — request logs export includes a replay token.
[04:10] [04:10] Maya: We'll share three failing request ids after the call.
[04:16] Priya: Encryption of logs in transit — do you encrypt exports to S3 with our KMS?
[04:21] Samir: Yes, server-side encryption with customer-managed KMS is supported. We also support HSM for Private deployments.
[04:28] [04:28] Ava: Now I'll demo a live debug — I'm pulling up a failing request. You'll see the request metadata on the right; the trace timeline in the center; at the bottom a raw request/response. Note: transcription sometimes shows 'redwood optimize' as 'redwood optima' in older transcripts — ignore that.
[04:50] [05:00] Ava: I'm toggling the 'show full request body' — this is permissioned by RBAC — watch how the UI highlights the token where output diverged from expected. We can add an annotation which becomes an action item in the trace.
[05:18] Daniel: Can you export a zip of all relevant logs? Our SRE will want the entire trace + system metrics.
[05:24] Ava: Yep, 'Export package' button creates a hash-signed zip with traces, request logs CSV, and perf metrics. You'll get a signed URL that expires in 48 hours.
[05:36] Maya: About pilot — can you provision a small Dedicated pool for us to run 10 requests/s sustained? We want to test tail latency under load.
[05:45] Samir: For pilot we can do a 3-month dedicated commit with burst to hosted. I'll include pricing in the proposal. For load tests we also provide a benchmark harness (link: benchmarks/nebula-template) so you can reproduce results.
[06:03] Ava: Quick note on debugging: sometimes model names in traces are mis-identified when we route to a quantized variant — the model_version label may show 'gptx-q4' instead of the full canonical name. We're working on making that clearer.
[06:20] [06:20] Priya: Any concerns on PII in request logs — we need to mask certain fields before storing.
[06:25] Ava: We have automatic redaction rules and you can supply custom regex masks client-side. We also provide hooks to redact before ingestion.
[06:33] Maya: Great. Walk me through how we would triage a spike in hallucinations — say in the last 24 hours.
[06:40] Ava: Use the Error Analysis 'regression' view — it groups by eval sets and prompts. You can pin a prompt set and see precision/recall metrics across model versions; we also alert on delta thresholds. We surface example requests and let you open the trace to see where generation started to drift.
[07:02] [07:02] Daniel: Is there an API to pull those regression metrics programmatically?
[07:06] Ava: Yes, we have a metrics API and a webhooks feed for regression alerts.
[07:12] [07:12] Jordan (CS): I'm going to note down next steps — Samir will send the security pack, Ava will run the replay, customer to share failing ids.
[07:20] Samir: Quick question on integrations — do you use Okta?
[07:24] Maya: Yes, Okta and internal SAML. We map groups to roles.
[07:29] Samir: Perfect, SAML S S O with Okta is a common setup, we'll include our SSO config guide.
[07:35] [08:00] Ava: Demo wrap up — watched the request replay, exported logs, configured RBAC view. A couple of UI notes: timestamp resolution in trace timeline currently rounds to nearest 10ms in some traces.
[08:16] Priya: For the compliance review we'll need an audit log of who accessed which request bodies. Is that captured?
[08:22] Ava: Yes, audit logs capture UI access (user, action, request_id, timestamp). We can stream audit logs to your SIEM as well.
[08:33] Maya: Would you be able to sign an addendum for data handling?
[08:36] Samir: We have standard DPA and can add clauses — our legal team can work with yours.
[08:45] [09:00] Ethan: One more question — can you run a synthetic test that replays a failing conversation across multiple sessions to reproduce cross-session state?
[09:08] Ava: We can, but we need the exact prompts and session keys. Best approach is to run the replay in a sandbox environment with snapshot KV cache attached. I'll coordinate with you on that.
[09:20] Jordan: I'm adding that as an action item for Ava.
[09:25] Samir: Ok, last bit — pricing for pilot and SLA. We offer pilot pricing with month-to-month for three months and then conversion discounts if you commit. I'll share a proposal.
[09:38] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks for the walkthrough. We'll send the failing ids and confirm pilot stakeholders.
[09:45] Samir: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the security docs and pilot proposal.
[09:51] Ava: Thanks, talk soon.
